candidate.name: identifier_quoting_normalizer
candidate.hypothesis: A deterministic, schema-derived backtick normalizer on outgoing execute_sql arguments will convert >=5 of the 17 budget-exhausted episodes and >=2 of the 12 premature commits into passes (accuracy 0.42 -> >=0.55), because those episodes already contain a corrected-candidate query; tokens drop >=40% since 82% of tokens burn in repeat-error loops.
candidate.changes: Response-side only. transform_response parses the table name and headers declared in the public user message ('The name of this table is X, and the headers of this table are H1,H2,...'), then backtick-quotes bare occurrences of declared identifiers that cannot be bare (chars outside [A-Za-z0-9_], or MySQL reserved words such as rank/order/group) inside outgoing execute_sql 'query' arguments. Rewrites skip string literals, already-quoted spans, qualified names (preceded by '.'), and function-call positions (followed by '('); longest identifiers are applied first. A same-mechanism sub-rule maps a trailing-punctuation header's bare core (e.g. 'No' for 'No.') back to the fully quoted declared form. transform_request is identity; commit_final_answer and all other fields are untouched; the response dict is copied, never mutated; behavior is identity when parsing fails or no declaration is present.
candidate.expected_efficiency: pass rate 0.42 -> 0.55-0.65; tokens 547509 -> ~250-300k (-45%); turns 367 -> ~230-260 (-30%), because the 17 turn-cap failures spend 82% of tokens retrying the verbatim failing SQL. Offline replay: 23/29 failing episodes have >=1 rewritten query; 7/21 passing episodes are rewritten only by adding backticks to already-correct declared identifiers.

candidate.name: declared_identifier_surface_normalizer
candidate.hypothesis: Canonicalizing declared identifiers to the engine's surface form -- (a) rewriting a whole double-quoted span whose stripped content case-insensitively equals a declared identifier into the backticked declared form, and (b) matching escape-embedded declared tokens (literal backslash whitespace escapes) with a whitespace-tolerant pattern and emitting the normalized single-space backticked form -- will turn the two remaining surface-form failures into passes and remove one recovery turn in two currently-passing episodes, lifting accuracy 0.52 -> ~0.56 (range 0.54-0.58), because a double-quoted identifier is silently read as a string constant by this engine (constant-false predicate instead of a column reference) and an escape-embedded header never matches the model's space-separated emission. Offline replay over the 50 public train episodes: 46/50 responses byte-identical to the incumbent, only 4 episodes change (one call each), so regression outside those 4 is impossible.
candidate.changes: Builds on agents/identifier_quoting_normalizer.py (round-1 incumbent, 0.52) as a standalone copy, response-side only. transform_response now first applies a double-quote canonicalization pass over the outgoing execute_sql 'query': scans spans respecting single-quote/backtick protection boundaries with doubled-quote and backslash escaping consistent with the existing mask scanner; a span whose stripped inner text case-insensitively equals a declared identifier is replaced by that identifier in backticks with the declaration's casing; exact whole-span match only; qualified-name and call-position contexts are skipped; unterminated quote runs untouched. Then a target-building addition: for declared identifiers containing a literal backslash-letter escape, an extra whitespace-tolerant target (word pieces joined by \s+, same edge guards) maps the model's space-separated surface to the backticked normalized single-space form; identifiers without escapes keep the incumbent's exact matching unchanged. The rewritten string then flows through the incumbent's bare-identifier quoting pass. All other behavior identical: transform_request identity; commit_final_answer arguments never touched; response deep-copied, never mutated; identity on unparseable declaration, no target firing, or any exception.
candidate.expected_efficiency: pass rate 0.52 -> 0.56 (range 0.54-0.58): recompute of corrected queries plausibly resolves the two surface-form failures and lets the model read real values in the double-quoted cases; the two passing episodes keep identical final SQL with one fewer error-recovery turn. Tokens 154,238 -> ~145,000 (-6%, mostly one episode's 22.5k error-loop episode shortening), turns 155 -> ~148.

candidate.name: text_toolcall_recovery
candidate.hypothesis: Promoting the model's text-form tool invocation into a real execute_sql call -- either a whole-content <tool_call> XML block whose embedded JSON the harness rejected as malformed, or the single fenced SQL block the harness never executes -- will convert the one deterministic 15-turn zero-execution episode (23,010 tokens, no statement ever run, malformed-XML loop) into an executing episode and remove one wasted recovery turn from six currently-passing episodes whose executed SQL is provably unchanged, lifting accuracy 0.54 -> 0.56 (range 0.54-0.56), because the failing episode already contains the exact statement the task needs but the host never runs it. Offline replay over the 50 public train episodes: only 9/50 episodes change at all, all 119 responses that already carry tool calls are byte-identical to the incumbent, and 6 of the 9 changed episodes are passes altered only by executing the same statement one turn earlier.
candidate.changes: Builds on agents/declared_identifier_surface_normalizer.py (round-2 incumbent, 0.54) as a standalone copy, response-side only. When the model reply carries no tool calls at all, transform_response attempts to recover at most one statement from response['content'] into a single execute_sql call: (1) XML form -- content is a whole-content <tool_call>{...}</tool_call> block; a body that parses as JSON is left untouched (the harness executes those itself and promoting would double-run); otherwise the body must name execute_sql, must have the documented shape (whitespace-stripped span between the name value and the 'query' key equals ',"arguments":{', rstripped body ends with '}}', tail before those braces ends with a quote), and the query value is sliced verbatim from the opening quote consumed by the key pattern through the last quote before the closing braces, preserving inner quotes and backslash escapes byte-for-byte; (2) fenced form -- exactly one ```/```sql/```mysql fence whose stripped body starts with a SQL keyword. In both forms the recovered text must start with a SQL keyword and contain at most one statement (semicolon scanner respecting quote spans, doubled-quote and backslash escapes). commit_final_answer is never synthesized. The recovered SQL is pushed through the incumbent's declared-identifier normalization (backtick quoting of non-bare declared identifiers, double-quote canonicalization, escape handling) before being emitted as dict(response) with one deterministic-id execute_sql call; content is untouched and inputs are never mutated. Responses that already carry tool calls take the incumbent path unchanged (commit_final_answer skipped, execute_sql arguments normalized). transform_request is identity; any exception, unparseable content, or ambiguity (multiple fences, concatenated XML blocks, parseable JSON block, non-SQL text) degrades to identity.
candidate.expected_efficiency: pass rate 0.54 -> 0.56 (one deterministic flip, bounded [0.54, 0.56]): the zero-execution episode begins executing its already-correct INSERT on turn 1 instead of looping 15 malformed-XML turns; the six passing fence episodes keep byte-identical executed SQL with one fewer recovery turn. Tokens 155,079 -> ~127-130k (-16 to -18%, the eliminated episode alone is 23k); turns 159 -> ~138 (-13%). Offline replay over evidence/candidate_02: 23/159 model responses change across 9/50 episodes (1203, 1779, 1790, 2211, 2491, 3028, 3215, 3922, 4197); 119/119 tool-call-bearing responses byte-identical to the incumbent; no input mutation; the two other failing fenced episodes execute the same statement they already ran one turn later, so their outcomes are semantically unchanged.

candidate.name: declared_surface_restoration
candidate.hypothesis: Restoring the public message's surface forms for tokens the model normalized -- (a) rebinding a declared identifier the model re-spelled with underscores or with a trailing parenthetical group dropped back to the declared name, and (b) restoring a value literal that lost the question's digit grouping or percent sign (or punctuation spacing) to the question's surface -- will convert the remaining surface-mismatch write failures into passes and remove one wasted recovery turn in the affected episodes, lifting accuracy 0.56 -> 0.58 (range 0.56-0.60), because the question text is generated from the gold cell surfaces, so a write that normalizes a formatted value to a bare number or drops a column name's unit suffix stores a value the checker cannot match, while an underscore-joined table spelling silently misses the real table; the outgoing execute_sql statement is the only place the runtime can restore those surfaces before execution.
candidate.changes: Builds on agents/text_toolcall_recovery.py (round-3 incumbent, 0.56) as a standalone copy, response-side only; transform_request stays identity. Facet A, inside _build_targets: for every declared identifier it computes the normalized surface N (literal backslash-letter escapes read as spaces, whitespace collapsed) and generates re-spelling variants -- the parenthetical-tail-dropped base (a declared name ending in a unit group loses that group) and every underscore-joined word prefix of N whose words are purely alphanumeric. A variant is admitted only when it is >= 6 chars, differs from N and from the declared token, and no other declared identifier's key (lowercase alphanumeric-only) is equal to it, a prefix of it, or has it as a prefix (this kills every overlapping-declared-name ambiguity class); admitted variants become targets replacing the bare variant with the backticked normalized declared surface. Variant targets are never applied to statements whose leading keyword is CREATE/ALTER/DROP; the incumbent's original targets still apply to every statement type. Facet B: _question_literals parses the public user message containing 'Question:', collecting quoted spans (straight or curly, inner 2-80 chars) and formatted numerics (digit-grouped, percent, dollar forms) and keeping only keys that have exactly one distinct surface. _restore_literals rewrites tokens only inside the value span of a value-writing statement (after the last VALUES for INSERT/REPLACE; between the first SET and the first WHERE for UPDATE, both located by a quote-aware scan), only for single-quoted literals and bare numerics outside backticked/double-quoted spans, and only when: the question gives one surface Q with the same alphanumeric key; Q differs from the literal; neither side contains backslash or quote characters; every non-alphanumeric character occurs no more often in the literal than in Q (the model may never add formatting the question lacks); and stripping trailing '.,;: ' from both does not make them equal (protects sentence-final punctuation). Rewrites replace the exact token span with the question's surface in single quotes. Literal restoration runs first, then the incumbent's double-quote canonicalization and bare-identifier quoting on the result; results are emitted as dict(response) with content byte-identical; commit_final_answer arguments are never touched; any exception, unparseable declaration, or ambiguity degrades to the original response. General-purpose throughout: no task names, ids, dataset-specific strings, or values in code or comments.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Pass rate 0.56 -> 0.58 (range 0.56-0.60). Verified offline replay over the 50 stored incumbent episodes (135 model responses, new transform vs incumbent applied to the raw stored responses with the episode history as public_history): exactly 6 responses change in 4 episodes -- 1113 t1 (UPDATE bare 900000/1.5/73.8 -> '900,000'/'1.5%'/'73.8%', the question's formatted surfaces; this is the flip claim, bounded by the gold cell preserving those surfaces), 4078 t1 and t3 (underscore-spelled table rebound to the declared table AND the date literal restored to the question's spacing before the comma; both rules fire in the same statement, so this second flip is joint), 3559 t2/t3 (bare parenthetical-dropped column name rebound to the backticked declared name, eliminating the two error turns, the DESCRIBE detour and the retries; accuracy effect NOT claimed -- the stored run eventually inserted all rows), 630 t1 (underscore-spelled table rebound; 630 already passes, so this removes one recovery turn only). Idempotence: re-applying the transform to its own output changes nothing (135/135). Zero input mutations, content byte-identical, outputs plain JSON-serializable dicts. Regression scan: 26/26 successful executed statements across the 28 passing episodes are byte-identical new-vs-incumbent (630's turn-1 statement is the only passing-episode statement touched, and it was the erroring one). Tokens 121,478 -> ~111-116k (-4 to -8%, mostly the 15,953-token error loop in 3559 collapsing to ~6.5k); turns 135 -> ~127 (3559 12 -> ~5, 630 3 -> 2). Every changed response is confined to an execute_sql query; no response that already carries correct statements is altered.

candidate.name: missing_table_repeat_probe
candidate.hypothesis: Substituting one read-only schema-listing probe (`SHOW TABLES;`) for the outgoing execute_sql call when the reply re-emits a statement whose most recent execution failed with a missing-table error (MySQL 1146 / "doesn't exist" / "unknown table") will convert 2 of the 27 failures (545, 759) to passes and remove ~24 turns / ~45k tokens, lifting accuracy 0.46 -> 0.50 (range 0.48-0.52), because both dead episodes re-emit the identical failing statement 14 times each and never commit, while in 5/5 episodes of this sample where the model actually saw the table list its very next emitted statement used the exact declared table surface; the probe never fires on a first emission, so its blast radius is confined to episodes already burning their budget on that exact repeat.
candidate.changes: Builds on agents/text_toolcall_recovery.py (retained incumbent, 0.46 on training sample 1) as a standalone copy, response-side only; transform_request stays identity. A probe check runs at the very top of transform_response, before the inherited has_calls / identifiers early returns, so it also works when no declaration parses. It fires only when ALL hold: response is a dict whose tool_calls is a list/tuple of exactly one call; that call's function name is execute_sql; no commit_final_answer appears anywhere in the response; the arguments (JSON string or dict) parse to a dict with a non-empty str query; and the query -- verbatim after strip, or after re-applying the inherited emission normalization (double-quote canonicalization + bare-identifier quoting with identifiers parsed from public_history) to match a statement that was actually executed -- equals a previously executed statement whose MOST RECENT paired tool result carries generic missing-table evidence (regex \b1146\b|doesn't exist|unknown table, applied only to engine error text, never to task/schema text). Prior executions are derived by walking public_history in order: each assistant message with exactly one execute_sql call is paired with its tool result (tool_call_id match preferred, immediately following role==tool message as fallback), keeping the latest result per distinct query text. On fire, it returns dict(response) with tool_calls replaced by one synthesized execute_sql call whose arguments are {"query": "SHOW TABLES;"}, reusing the original call id and type (deterministic FNV-1a id / "function" only if absent); the original content field and every other response field stay byte-identical; inputs are never mutated. Non-firing replies fall through to the inherited logic unchanged; any exception, ambiguity, missing history, or unparseable argument degrades to the original response. Stateless (no module-level mutable state), no I/O, imports unchanged (copy/json/re at module scope), and no task-specific strings, IDs, or instance-level values anywhere in code or comments.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Pass rate 0.46 -> 0.50 central (range 0.48-0.52; floor 0.46 if the model ignores the probe, ceiling 0.52). Verified offline replay over the 50 stored incumbent episodes (190 model calls, new transform vs incumbent applied to the stored responses with the stored request messages as public_history): the probe fires in exactly 5 episodes / 35 responses -- 545 x14 (t2-t15), 759 x14 (t2-t15), 145 x3 (t2-t4), 302 x3 (t2-t4), 2819 x1 (t2) -- and nowhere else; 2953 (1064 syntax loop) and 4296 (1064) get 0 fires by design; all 155 non-firing responses are deep-equal to the incumbent's output; 0/190 inputs mutated; 35/35 fired outputs keep content and identity fields with exactly one {"query": "SHOW TABLES;"} call. The two 15-turn zero-commit loops are 52,684 tokens combined (24% of the run) and their repeated statements are otherwise correct except the table surface, so the probe at t2 lets the model read the real table list and re-issue the corrected SELECT plus commit (as it did in 5/5 self-probed episodes), while 145/302 collapse 2-3 loop turns each (still failing on answer semantics, not claimed as flips). Total tokens 219,936 -> ~175k (-20%), turns 190 -> ~166 (-13%).

candidate.name: missing_table_surface_rebind
candidate.hypothesis: Replacing the blind SHOW TABLES; probe payload with a declared-table-surface rebind (fired only when a re-emitted statement's most recent execution failed with a missing-table error that names a token whose alphanumeric key equals exactly one declared identifier's key) breaks the inherited probe's verbatim-retry deadlock: in the episodes where the probe re-fires 13-14 times at 13-14k tokens each, the repaired statement executes for real and the model sees a fresh engine outcome (rows, or an empty result) instead of a schema listing it has already seen, including the one task the round-5 probe regressed from pass to fail. This lifts round-6 pass rate 0.50 -> 0.52 (range 0.50-0.54) and removes ~40k tokens / ~42 turns with zero change to any response the incumbent does not already probe.
candidate.changes: Standalone copy of agents/missing_table_repeat_probe.py, response-side only; transform_request stays identity. _probe_response(response, call) was generalized into _substitute_response(response, call, query) (same call id/type preservation and JSON arguments form; _probe_response remains a one-line alias for the SHOW TABLES; probe). New _MISSING_TABLE_NAME_RES mines the failing table spelling from the paired tool-result text only (two engine wordings; surrounding backticks stripped; schema prefix before the first '.' dropped), _alnum_key is a case- and punctuation-insensitive comparison key, and _rebind_missing_table(query, identifiers, error_text) returns None unless: the normalized statement does not start with CREATE/ALTER/DROP, a token is mined, its key is >= 3 chars, and exactly one declared identifier's key matches and differs textually from the failing spelling. On success it scans _comparison_text(query, identifiers) left-to-right, skipping single-quoted spans with the inherited backslash/doubled-quote rule, substituting identifier-position occurrences of the failing spelling (case-insensitive, optional surrounding backtick, occurrences preceded by '.' or an identifier char or followed by an identifier char are skipped; matches already reading as the backticked declared surface are left alone) with the declared identifier backticked; the repaired text is not re-normalized. In _missing_table_repeat_probe the repair is attempted first inside the existing match loop and returned via _substitute_response; when no unambiguous repair exists the inherited _probe_response fires exactly as before; all other reply classes fall through unchanged. Shallow copies only, inputs never mutated, no commit or non-execute_sql field touched, no module state, no I/O, imports unchanged (copy/json/re), no task names, ids, table names or instance strings in code or comments.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Pass rate 0.50 -> 0.52 central (floor 0.50, ceiling 0.54). Verified offline replay over all 202 stored incumbent (candidate_05) model calls, new transform vs incumbent on the same raw responses with the stored executed history as public_history: exactly 42 responses change across exactly 5 episodes (2181 t3-t15 x13, 302 t2-t15 x14, 545 t3-t15 x13, 759 t2 x1, 2819 t2 x1); all 42 are responses the incumbent had already replaced with its SHOW TABLES; payload, and the repair emits the model's own intended statement with the declared identifier backticked (independently re-verified); 160/160 non-firing responses byte-identical to the incumbent; 0 changes where the incumbent returned identity; idempotence 202/202; input mutations 0. Token/turn: the three deadlocked episodes burn 52.2k tokens / 45 turns on 13-14 probe substitutions each; collapsing them into real executions is expected to cut the run total ~228k -> ~188k tokens and ~202 -> ~160 turns even in the floor case, and the recorded counterexample for 2181 shows the repaired statement's result reproduces the exact passing execution path from its round-5 baseline.
